goal.what: A deliverable that a builder makes by a kind's practice, and an evaluator passes by its standard alone, serves the purpose of the one who uses it.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md: "The Standard alone evaluates the deliverable"
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md, Three best practices: "meta ... fit for its purpose"

decisions.what: Who uses a best practice, and for what?
decisions.decided: The builder makes a deliverable by the practice; the evaluator judges it by the standard; both are AIs. The user approves the kind's goal and questions.
Who uses a deliverable of the kind, in what moment, and what they get with it, so that the builder and the evaluator settle from it any point nothing else settles, and the user judges the kind by it.
grounds: Brookhart, "Appropriate Criteria: Key to Effective Rubrics", Frontiers in Education, 2018: "True rubrics feature criteria appropriate to an assessment's purpose"

decisions.what: What must hold for the standard to judge right?
decisions.decided: It passes a deliverable exactly when its user gets what the goal says.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md: "a deliverable that answers every question yes is done, and nothing more is added"

decisions.what: Where do the questions come from?
decisions.decided: From the goal, split down by asking what must hold for its user, until each condition is answered yes or no; the conditions become the questions' checks, and like conditions are merged into one question. Questions are not matched one to one with the template's parts.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md, planner 4-5: "Write the leaf conditions as the Checklist's questions"

decisions.what: How is it known that no question is needless?
decisions.decided: Each question asks something the goal needs; one that the goal does not need is cut.
grounds: Brookhart, "Appropriate Criteria: Key to Effective Rubrics", Frontiers in Education, 2018: "True rubrics feature criteria appropriate to an assessment's purpose"

decisions.what: How is it known that no question repeats another?
decisions.decided: Each question asks what no other asks; where two would fail the same deliverables for the same reason, they are one.

decisions.what: How is it known that nothing the user needs is missed?
decisions.decided: A deliverable that its users found short fails some question; real deliverables are judged, and a question is added or mended where one found short passes.
grounds: Shankar et al., "Who Validates the Validators?", arXiv:2404.12272, 2024: "users need criteria to grade outputs, but grading outputs helps users define criteria."
Anthropic, "Demystifying evals for AI agents", anthropic.com/engineering, 2026: "Converting user-reported failures into test cases ensures your suite reflects actual usage"

decisions.what: How do two evaluators reach the same answer?
decisions.decided: Each question is set in a scene of use and rests on checks answered yes or no, with an example that fails and one that passes where the words could pass what misses the aim.
grounds: Anthropic, "Demystifying evals for AI agents", anthropic.com/engineering, 2026: "A good task is one where two domain experts would independently reach the same pass/fail verdict."
Lee et al., "CheckEval", arXiv:2403.18771v2: "We create Boolean questions that correspond to the sub-dimensions defined in the first step."

decisions.decided: The deliverable and the standard alone, as the deliverable's user meets only the deliverable.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md: "The Standard alone evaluates the deliverable"

decisions.what: What must hold for the practice to build right?
decisions.decided: A builder who follows it makes a deliverable that passes the standard.

decisions.what: How does the builder know where each thing goes?
decisions.decided: The template gives the deliverable's shape, each part with what it holds and whom it serves, in the order its user meets it.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md: "Template: the shape its readers expect, so they find each part where they look for it."

decisions.what: How does the builder know how to make each question yes?
decisions.decided: Each question has one method: steps in order, one action each, naming the part it writes.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md: "Methods: a proven way for each question of the Checklist"

decisions.what: How is a method known to work?
decisions.decided: Each step rests on a source, quoted from a page opened, where the way has worked, or is said to be reasoning; the method is tried on a real deliverable and mended where its question stays no.
grounds: Shankar et al., "Who Validates the Validators?", arXiv:2404.12272, 2024: "users need criteria to grade outputs, but grading outputs helps users define criteria."

decisions.what: Where do questions shared by kinds live?
decisions.decided: Once, in refactor-doc or refactor-code, named in includes; a script checks it, so it is no question of meta.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md, Files: "A question copied into each kind would be mended in one and left old in the rest."

decisions.what: How does the user judge the goal and the questions on one reading?
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md, Three best practices: "refactor-doc, how a document says what it says: understood as meant, on one reading."
